decisions.reason: No prior adjudication or state files exist for this work. In this prospective OSF registration, Rachev explicitly registers a new-participant Bulgarian experiment to retest specific empirical findings from Rinck et al. (2001) alongside Bransford et al. (1972) and Jahn (2004): Confirmatory Hypothesis 1 tests the model-type (same/different) by probe-type (old/new) interaction reported by Bransford et al. (1972) and Rinck et al. (2001), Confirmatory Hypothesis 2 tests the main effect of model type for new sentences reported by Rinck et al. (2001) and Jahn (2004), discriminability (d') is computed following Rinck (2001), and the sample size of 50 is explicitly benchmarked against the 48 participants of Rinck et al. (2001). Although Rinck et al. (2001) was itself an earlier replication in the chain from Bransford et al. (1972), it reported distinct empirical results (discrimination between old and new probes with a model-type effect restricted to new sentences and d' analyses) that this registration directly retests. The reference list (q23) and Crossref metadata identify the source-backed citation as Rinck, M., Hähnel, A., & Becker, G. (2001), 'Using temporal information to construct, update, and retrieve situation models of narratives', Journal of Experimental Psychology: Learning, Memory, and Cognition, 27(1), 67-80 (10.1037/0278-7393.27.1.67). It is absent from the sole shipped row (input_row_index 0: Bransford et al., 1972, 10.1016/0010-0285(72)90003-5) and distinct from sibling target_index 2 (Jahn, 2004, 10.1037/0278-7393.30.5.969); report equivalence does not apply.

decisions.quote: To address these limitations, in 2022 I designed an online experiment closely following Jahn's (2004, Experiment 1) design and using Jahn's stimulus sentences translated into Bulgarian). Administration was individual and the order of sentences randomized. Unlike Bransford et al. (1972), I found no significant model type (same/different) by probe type (old/new) interaction effect on the recognition scores. Unlike Rinck et al. (2001), the main effect of model type for new sentences was not significant, although it was in the expected direction. Unlike Jahn (2004) there was no significant model type by scene type (predator/peaceful) interaction effect on recognition scores. Due to a bug in the experiment script, some sentence groups occurred more often than others. Now I aim to replicate Bransford et al.'s, Rinck et al.'s, and Jahn's results, with a new improved script and with a new set of participants.
decisions.reason: No prior adjudication or state files exist for this work. This prospective OSF registration closely follows the design and translated stimulus sentences of Jahn (2004, Experiment 1) in a new Bulgarian sample and explicitly retests Jahn's empirical findings: Confirmatory Hypothesis 2 tests the model-type main effect on new sentences (following Rinck et al., 2001 and Jahn, 2004) and Confirmatory Hypothesis 3 tests Jahn's (2004) specific model-type (same/different) by scene-type (predator/peaceful) interaction on new sentences. The reference list (q23) and Crossref metadata establish the original identity as Jahn, G. (2004), 'Three turtles in danger: Spontaneous construction of causally relevant spatial situation models', Journal of Experimental Psychology: Learning, Memory, and Cognition, 30(5), 969-987 (10.1037/0278-7393.30.5.969). The only shipped row is Bransford et al. (1972) (input_row_index 0, 10.1016/0010-0285(72)90003-5), which is an independent earlier study by different authors that did not test the predator/peaceful causal relevance manipulation, and sibling target_index 1 (Rinck et al., 2001, 10.1037/0278-7393.27.1.67) is a separate study; report equivalence does not apply.
